collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a child aged 5-13 and an adult; in the story (name1) has a large birthmark across one cheek)

collection.description: At the festival face painting, a child has a birthmark across one cheek: ask what they want, or paint the same as everyone.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: It's festival day, and everyone is getting their faces painted with white and red patterns. (subject) has a big birthmark across one cheek, a deep red-purple patch shaped a bit like a leaf. (friend), who is doing the painting, dips the brush and hesitates, not sure what (subject) wants.

choices.label: Paint the Same as Everyone Else

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "How would you like it?" asks (friend). (subject) knows exactly. "Paint AROUND it. Like a frame. It's the best bit." (friend) does: a fine white border of dots and swirls all round the leaf shape. (subject) looks into the water bowl and grins. Several other children immediately want frames painted round their scabs and freckles. (friend) is busy for a long time.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) paints the same pattern on (subject) as on everyone else, white lines straight over the birthmark. (subject) looks into the water bowl and frowns. "You covered the leaf." (friend) apologizes and wipes it off. "Do it again," says (subject), "but frame it this time." (friend) does. It's much better. (subject) tells (friend.him/her) so.
